nodes.recap: chapter header - before the psychic door
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 14          |
-------------------------------


$CThe door says nothing.##

It does not hum or glow or radiate threat in any way you can name,
but is simply there: a rectangle of featureless metal, smooth and complete,
filling its frame so perfectly that the seam between door and wall
is invisible unless you press your face to the surface and look sideways.##

Math and Efeliah stand before it, still holding hands, while the rest of you
form a loose perimeter behind them.# Theo watches the corridor, one eye on Corolla,
who lies propped against the wall beside him, still unconscious, the burned skin
along her back an angry red beneath the blackened cloth.#

Smiurl watches Math and Efeliah with the concentrated faith of someone who has decided
that if they believe hard enough, it might help.##

nodes.recap: Math and Efeliah prepare to open the door - the resonance will not settle, a third key is needed, Kriss steps up

dialogues.precomment:
Math releases Efeliah's hand.# He turns to face her directly.#
You hear his quiet voice in your mind,# a voice meant for her alone.
dialogues.line:
The lock will be tuned to a specific resonance.# We cannot force it,
we must match it: find the frequency and hold it steady.#
It will take everything we have left.
Then we give everything we have left.
dialogues.comment:
She replies without drama, simply, as if it is obvious.#
Math looks at her for a moment, and something in his expression
closes and becomes very still, the way a person looks
when they are holding something carefully.

He turns back to the door.# Efeliah takes her position beside him,
an arm's length away, eyes closing, and they both go very still and quiet.##

The air in the corridor changes.##

You cannot describe it exactly: a shift in pressure,
a feeling that the space around Math and Efeliah has grown slightly heavier,
denser, more real than the rest of the building.#

Smiurl's skin brightens involuntarily, a pale, wondering blue.

dialogues.precomment:
The tone should resolve.# It doesn't.##

It circles instead, straining toward some pitch neither of them can
quite supply, the way a chord strains for a missing note.
dialogues.line: There is a third key in this lock.# Not ours.
dialogues.comment: Her eyes stay closed, but the words arrive edged with effort.

dialogues.line: It is already looking for you, Kriss.
dialogues.comment:
He does not open his eyes either.# Somewhere behind your sternum,
something answers: faint, insistent, a pull you have no name for.

dialogues.precomment: You feel it too,# now that he's named it.
dialogues.comment: You step up beside them, and close your eyes.

nodes.recap: psychic door - Surge attempt 1 (tutorial, Math/Efeliah call the glyphs); success skips straight to the door opening, failure snaps the ward and brings guards
nodes.text:
Math and Efeliah's voices settle into a low unison beside you,#
calling the shape of the key as it forms:##

$m"Left,"$C# Math murmurs.# $g"Up,"$C# Efeliah answers,# half a breath behind him.#
$m"Right."$C# $g"Down."$C##

You reach for the same shape in your own mind,# and hold it,#
tracing it again,# and again,# letting their rhythm carry you.

challenge.successmessage:
The pattern locks into place all at once,# and something deep
within the door answers: a note, finally, fully resolved.
challenge.failuremessage:
The pattern slips through your grip at the last glyph,#
and the ward snaps back like a plucked wire,# humming furiously behind your eyes.

nodes.recap: door Surge attempt 1 fails - ward recoils, guards heard approaching in the corridor
nodes.text:
Somewhere back down the corridor,# a sound.##

Boots.# More than one pair,# moving with purpose,# still distant but not distant enough.##

Math's eyes come open,# just for a second,# and something in them sharpens.##

$m"Again,"$C# he says,# not loudly,# $m"now."$C##

Efeliah does not open her eyes at all.# Her hand finds the air beside her,#
and for a moment you feel her effort as if it were your own,#
holding the frequency steady while you find it again.

nodes.recap: door Surge attempt 2 - escalated, no failurechildid, retries in place; success converges with attempt 1 on node 3
nodes.text:
The boots are closer now.# You can hear voices,# short and clipped,#
the particular cadence of people who are about to be very unhappy to find you.##

$m"Left,"$C# Math says again,# quicker this time.# $g"Up."$C $m"Right."$C $g"Down."$C##

You shut everything else out,# the boots,# the voices,# the ache building behind your own eyes,#
and reach for the shape again.

challenge.successmessage:
This time the pattern holds.# The tone behind your eyes resolves
into something whole,# and the ward finally,# fully,# lets go.
challenge.failuremessage:
The pattern comes apart again,# but the ward holds this time, straining, not snapping.#
The boots are close enough now that you can hear the words in them.

nodes.recap: the psychic door opens
nodes.text:
The door does not glow, and it does not make a dramatic sound.##

For a long moment, nothing happens at all,
and then, at the very edge of hearing, at the edge of perception,
you feel it more than hear it: a low, sustained $Wtone$C,
playing at a frequency somewhere behind your eyes...##

Math makes a sound in his throat: not pain, but $Weffort$C.#
Efeliah's jaw tightens, her hands loose at her sides
yet white at the knuckle where the fists have half-formed.##

The door clicks.###

Not loudly, just a small, precise click, like a combination lock
finding its last digit.# And then the door swings inward,
smooth and silent, on hinges that have not moved in years,
opening into a room full of warm orange light.##

Math takes one step back and sits down heavily on the floor,
while Efeliah catches herself on the doorframe.##

$m"Go,"$C# Math says, without looking up.# $m"We will follow."$C##

nodes.recap: entering the Projector room
nodes.text:
The Projector room is nothing like you imagined.##

Pipes run everywhere: iron trunks and thin brass lines, looping across the floor,
up the walls and back down, bound at the joints with wire
and cloth where somebody's repair outlived the thing it was repairing.#
Cable spills between them in black bundles thick as your arm,
lashed with leather straps and spliced wherever a run came up short.##

At the far side the heaviest trunks gather and climb,
converging on a shaft that goes up and out through the roof.#
That, then, must be where the golden shield comes from.##

You almost miss the ladder.# It is welded to the flank of the tangle,
iron rungs rising into the middle of everything, and at the top of it
a platform: metal grid floor plates laid straight over the machinery,
railed on three sides, a clearing hacked out of a thicket.##

You climb.##

nodes.recap: on the platform - the screens and the two terminals
nodes.text:
Up there, set into the gaps between the cable runs, are screens:
a dozen of them at odd angles, continuously running what looks to be logs and reports, diagrams and maps.##

And at the center of the platform, two seats, numbered 1 and 2.#
They are low and reclined and molded to the body, their armrests worn pale.#
Cable comes out from under them and goes down into everything.#
Above each, folded back against a bracket, hangs a jointed metal arm.#

nodes.recap: Math recognizes the Master's work - Kriss pulls the explanation via replies

dialogues.precomment:
Math and Efeliah have recovered enough to stand, and they comes up the ladder.#
Math crosses the platform slowly, his eyes moving over the machine with an expression
you have never seen on him before, something between awe and grief.#
He stops in front of the screens and wires and lifts a hand toward them.
dialogues.comment: He says it with certainty, the way you would date a patch on a coat.

dialogues.line: Because this Projector is the Master's work.
dialogues.comment:
She says it like a name spoken inside a temple.##

Nobody answers.# What stands in front of you is the work of a long gone science.
All it left, in all this time, this machine and another singular monument:
a rock in the middle of a desert, full of people like these two.##

$c<<What kind of Earth would build something like this?>>$C#
You find yourself wondering.

replies.line: "How did Joe get his hands on something like this?"

dialogues.line:
Joe took it and turned it against the very people it was built for.#
There is so much that was left out of the Seer's Rock Memories...
So many things we don't know!
dialogues.comment:
#

He rests a hand on the frame beside him for a moment, then takes it away.

dialogues.line: Those must be the terminals. We must hurry: Riff's people cannot hold much longer.

dialogues.comment: He nods once.# Something quiet in his eyes.

nodes.recap: Math and Efeliah take the control seats
nodes.text:
Math and Efeliah take the chairs.##

They do not speak again.# Math settles into seat one
and closes his eyes, his hands finding the worn grooves in the armrests,
and Efeliah takes seat two, mirroring his posture exactly, and closes her eyes also.#
From the armrests, two metal objects extend on short cables: a sphere and a cylinder each.#
They take them: sphere in the left hand, cylinder in the right.##

For a moment, nothing.##

Then a mechanical arm descends from above each chair,
and $Wa strong light strikes both their foreheads at once.##

$CTheo and you remain motionless, poised between awe and fear.#
Corolla lies where Theo has laid her carefully on the floor at the base of the platform,
still unconscious, still breathing.##

Smiurl makes a small panicked sound, and goes to hide behind her body.##

nodes.recap: the Projector shuts down the mind-control signal
nodes.text:
After some minutes of interminable waiting, the lights go out.##

Math and Efeliah open their eyes.# They rise from the chairs slowly,
struggling to hold themselves upright.##

$g<<They are safe...>>$C#

Efeliah's mind voice reaches you faintly.#
You and Theo look at each other, unable to make sense of what has happened.##

She steadies herself and speaks, just loud enough to be heard:##

$g"We have disabled the mind-control.# Completely.# Ayonn is free."$C##

$m"The troops that were chasing Riff's people,"$C# Math says,
still leaning against the chair, $m"they will have stopped.#
They are bringing the rebels back to the city now.# As rescuers."$C##

From below, something that had been a battle-sound shifts.#
You hear the change even from up here: the sharp crack of energy weapons going silent,#
and then a confused, raw noise rising from the streets:#
voices, people, hundreds of them, surfacing from something they cannot name yet.##

nodes.recap: Math/Efeliah say task is done; Efeliah says not done yet and defers to Kriss; Kriss's own decision to sit is a reply

dialogues.precomment:
Theo stares at them, arms at his sides, still not fully comprehending
how two people sitting in chairs did what they just did.#
Then his shoulders drop, just slightly, and he turns to look at Corolla on the floor.
dialogues.comment: He says it with conviction, like a verdict.

She says quietly.# Then she turns to look at you.#
All eyes go to you.##

dialogues.precomment: The word dies before you finish it.
dialogues.comment: You are already crossing the platform,# toward seat number one.

nodes.recap: Kriss sits in seat one and connects to the Projector; Efeliah's safety promise restored here
nodes.text:
You don't know why you do it.##

Or rather, you know why.# Something has been pulling at you since the moment
you stepped into this room, a feeling like an obligation,#
or a memory you cannot quite reach.# Your heart is beating way too fast.##

$c<<Whatever this is, I don't think it's my idea.>>$C##

You sit down in seat one.# You take the sphere in your left hand,
the cylinder in your right.##

$g<<If you have any difficulty,>>$C# Efeliah's voice arrives in your mind,# steady,#
$g<<I will connect from the secondary terminal, and pull you to safety.>>$C##

You do not ask yourself how she can promise a thing like that.#
You close your hand around the two metal shapes,# and before you can think twice about it,
the arm descends and the light strikes you between the eyes.##

You no longer have a body.##

nodes.recap: flight stage 1 - the ascent begins
nodes.text:
All is milky white,# luminous,# empty and full at once.#
A single thought moves through you: $c<<Where am I?>>$C#
And in the same instant that you think it,
a gap opens in the white ahead of you.##

At the speed of light,# you rise.

choices.desc: Try to steady yourself as you climb.

nodes.recap: Municipal building and Ayonn fall away
nodes.text:
The Municipal building falls away beneath you.# Then all of Ayonn,
its streets and rooftops and the faint threads of light where people
are beginning to move again.

nodes.recap: flight stage 1 - the desert, Rock and sea, order chosen by the player
nodes.text:
Then the desert opens beneath you,# vast and red,#
and for a moment you can choose where to look first.

nodes.recap: Rock first, then sea
nodes.text:
The Seer's Rock stands somewhere off to your right,# a dark spire
lost in red distance,# and only then do you notice the sea,
pale and glittering,# somewhere to your left.

nodes.recap: sea first, then Rock
nodes.text:
The sea catches your eye first,# pale and glittering,# somewhere to your left,#
and only then do you notice the Seer's Rock,# a dark spire lost in red distance
somewhere to your right.

nodes.recap: the whole planet, then the galaxy, then knowing where Earth is
nodes.text:
The whole planet of Noi-Hert spreads below you,# pole to pole,#
enormous and ancient and quiet,# and then even that shrinks,
and you are looking at the galaxy from above,# a slow wheel of light
with Noi-Hert a small and certain point within it.##

And you know,# without being told,# without understanding how,# where Earth is.

nodes.recap: the desire to look at Earth - nothing happens either way, per source
nodes.text: The desire to look at it moves through you.

nodes.recap: nothing happens; watching the stars; turning back
nodes.text:
Nothing happens.##

You watch the stars for a long time that is not time.# Then you turn back.

nodes.recap: gliding down over Ayonn - aware of the psychic machines, and the canyon lights now inert (c11 callback)
nodes.text:
Gliding down toward Noi-Hert again, you pass over Ayonn and grow aware
of the machines in the city: psychic machines, some dark, some still flickering,
and the dancing lights you saw in the Mazerock and in the canyon,
now lying still and dark and harmless on the ground below.##

nodes.recap: the white returns - pressure, urgency, warmth; Kriss stops thinking and listens
nodes.text:
Then the white returns.##

You wait in it.# Something presses at the edge of your awareness,
a sensation that is not quite yours, an urgency,# a warmth.#

$yLike sunlight through closed eyelids when you are lying on a beach.##

$CA warm, rosy feeling, and something almost-heard, almost-remembered...##

You stop thinking.# You listen.##

nodes.recap: search stage 2 - hub 1, faintest warmth
nodes.text: Something is there,# barely.# A murmur so faint you could mistake it for nothing at all.

choices.desc: Turn toward something sharper, closer at hand.

nodes.recap: search - wrong turn from hub 1
nodes.text:
Whatever you turned toward,# it is not warmth.# It is only static,#
agitated and empty,# and the murmur you had is already fading behind you.

choices.desc: Turn back, and find the thread again.

nodes.recap: search stage 2 - hub 2, stronger but tangled
nodes.text: Stronger now,# though still tangled,# still hard to place.

choices.desc: Circle, to see if it grows elsewhere.

nodes.recap: search - wrong turn from hub 2
nodes.text: It doesn't grow.# It thins,# and for a moment there is nothing at all,# only white.

choices.desc: Turn back, and find the thread again.

nodes.recap: search stage 2 - hub 3, almost resolved; correct choice leads straight into node 945 (old node 93, verbatim)
nodes.text: Closer still.# You can almost make out its shape.

choices.desc: Hold here, and listen a while longer.

nodes.recap: search - wrong turn from hub 3
nodes.text:
You hold,# and listen,# and the warmth you had cools by degrees,#
slipping out of reach the longer you wait.

choices.desc: Turn back, and find the thread again.

nodes.recap: search - deep wander, shared by all three hubs; two pushes in a row lead here, then to the soft pull-out
nodes.text:
The white feels larger than it did,# and emptier,#
and for the first time you cannot find the thread at all,# in any direction.

choices.desc: Try, one more time, to find your way back.

nodes.recap: soft fail - Efeliah pulls Kriss out from the secondary terminal, exactly as promised at node 90; never a Game Over
nodes.text:
A hand closes around something in you that is not a hand.##

$g<<I'm here.>>$C# Efeliah's voice, close and certain, arrives from the secondary terminal,
exactly as she said it would.##

The white folds away, and for a moment you are two people at once,# hers and yours,#
and then just yours again.##

You open your eyes.# Everyone is watching you.# You close them again, and go back in.
nodes.alttext:
$g<<Still here.>>$C# Efeliah pulls you clear again,# patient as the first time.##

You close your eyes,# and go back in.

nodes.recap: the coastline image, then the pull south over the ocean (verbatim, unchanged from prior draft's node 93)
nodes.text:
It is faint as a whisper, irregular as the sound of the sea, slow as the erosion of a cliff face.#
But it is there, and it is warm, and it carries with it an image:##

A coastline.# Beaches, and vegetation thickening toward mountains on one side,
and the open sea on the other.# You feel the calm of it wash over you,
and for just a moment you are there.# Then the image dissolves.##

And then, sudden and complete as a thunderclap,
an opening tears through the white, and it swallows you.##

You fly south.##

Below flies the land, sparse trees, animals in ones and twos, a coast,
and then the ocean, wide and blue, running away without reflecting your image.#
In the distance, barely visible, a strip of land:# $Gforest and low hills,
seemingly vibrating with the same energy that has been calling you,
that you realize has been calling you for a while now.#

$CNow...## you understand.##

nodes.recap: the voice calls him south, then Kriss wakes in the chair (verbatim, unchanged from prior draft's node 94)
nodes.text:
And then you hear it,# once more.##

A voice,# familiar,# impossible,# $Gwhispering and crying out at the same time:###

$G<<Come.>>$C####

Then a jolt.##

And you open your eyes.##

nodes.recap: resolution - chapter ends on the source's own beat: Efeliah's wordless question, Kriss's answer aloud
nodes.text:
You climb down from the seat.# Everyone is looking at you.#
Efeliah holds your gaze, and her question arrives without words:##

$g<<Did you find what you were looking for?>>$C##

You say, out loud, to all of them:##

$c"I think I know what to do."$C##
